## Overview

This document was generated on **`r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`**. It demonstrates how to transform multi-dimensional categorical data into a continuous visual stream using a **Sankey diagram** rendered via `plotly` in R.

Sankey diagrams excel at illustrating proportional shifts across categorical stages. Here, we track passenger demographics and survival outcomes from the RMS Titanic disaster of April 1912.

---

## Dataset Description

The analysis uses the built-in R `Titanic` dataset, derived from the official passenger manifest and historical records compiled after the sinking.

### Structure & Dimensions

The dataset is a 4-dimensional cross-tabulated array consisting of **2,201 records** categorized across four factors:

* **`Class`**: Passenger booking class or crew designation (*1st*, *2nd*, *3rd*, *Crew*).
* **`Sex`**: Biological sex (*Male*, *Female*).
* **`Age`**: Age category (*Child*, *Adult*).
* **`Survived`**: Final survival status (*No*, *Yes*).

### Data Summary

The table below aggregates the total passenger counts across passenger class, sex, and final survival outcomes:

```{r data-summary}
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

# Convert 4D array to data frame
titanic_df <- as.data.frame(Titanic) %>%
  filter(Freq > 0)

# Summary table grouped by Class, Sex, and Survived
summary_table <- titanic_df %>%
  group_by(Class, Sex, Survived) %>%
  summarise(Passengers = sum(Freq), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(Class, Sex, Survived)

kable(summary_table, caption = "Titanic Manifest Summary by Class, Sex, and Outcome")

```

---

## Interactive Flow Diagram

The Sankey diagram maps categorical transitions left-to-right along a two-stage flow:

$$\text{Passenger Class} \longrightarrow \text{Sex} \longrightarrow \text{Survival Outcome}$$

Hover over nodes or connecting flows to inspect exact passenger volumes.

```{r plotly-sankey, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
library(plotly)

# Stage 1: Class -> Sex
flow_class_sex <- titanic_df %>%
  group_by(Class, Sex) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(Freq), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(source_name = Class, target_name = Sex)

# Stage 2: Sex -> Survived
flow_sex_survived <- titanic_df %>%
  group_by(Sex, Survived) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(Freq), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(source_name = Sex, target_name = Survived) %>%
  mutate(target_name = paste("Outcome:", target_name))

# Combine stage flows
all_flows <- bind_rows(flow_class_sex, flow_sex_survived)

# Map nodes to 0-indexed vectors for Plotly
unique_nodes <- c("1st", "2nd", "3rd", "Crew", 
                  "Male", "Female", 
                  "Outcome: No", "Outcome: Yes")

node_lookup <- setNames(seq(0, length(unique_nodes) - 1), unique_nodes)

all_flows <- all_flows %>%
  mutate(
    source = node_lookup[source_name],
    target = node_lookup[target_name]
  )

# Define node palette
node_colors <- c(
  "#2b5c8f", "#3690c0", "#67a9cf", "#a6bddb", # Class nodes
  "#8856a7", "#e08214",                      # Sex nodes
  "#d73027", "#1a9850"                       # Survival outcome nodes
)

# Render Sankey Widget
plot_ly(
  type = "sankey",
  orientation = "h",
  node = list(
    label = unique_nodes,
    color = node_colors,
    pad = 18,
    thickness = 22,
    line = list(color = "#333333", width = 0.5)
  ),
  link = list(
    source = all_flows$source,
    target = all_flows$target,
    value  = all_flows$value
  )
) %>%
  layout(
    title = list(text = "Titanic Passenger Flows: Class → Sex → Survival", font = list(size = 16)),
    font = list(size = 12)
  )

```

---

## Analytical Observations

1. **Class Distribution**: Crew members and 3rd-class passengers represented the largest initial node blocks in the manifest.
2. **Gender Ratio**: Male passengers heavily outnumbered female passengers, particularly among crew members and 3rd-class travelers.
3. **Outcome Disparities**: The path width leading into **Outcome: Yes** illustrates high survival proportions among female passengers, highlighting the historical enforcement of the "women and children first" protocol during evacuation.
